name: Google Cloud Run

modes.label: Services, instance-based billing ("CPU always allocated"), Tier 1
modes.note: $0.000018/vCPU-s, $0.000002/GiB-s; whole instance lifetime billed, 1-minute minimum; no per-request fee. Tier 1 includes us-central1/us-east1/us-east4, europe-north1/west1/west4/southwest1/west9, asia-south1/northeast1/east1. GPU non-zonal-redundant L4 $0.0001867/s, RTX PRO 6000 $0.00036522/s. Cloud Run Jobs (run-to-completion tasks, up to 168 h/task) bill at these same instance-based rates with a 1-minute minimum; the separate jobs regime was merged here (identical price).

modes.label: Services, request-based billing (default), Tier 1
modes.note: No GPUs on request-based billing: Cloud Run docs say 'You must use instance-based billing to use the GPU feature' (GPU map removed 2026-09-28). Active rate $0.000024/vCPU-s, $0.0000025/GiB-s only while starting, shutting down or serving >= 1 request (rounded up to 100 ms) + $0.40 per 1M requests (start_fee assumes one request per session). Idle non-min instances free; min-instances idle at $0.0000025/vCPU-s + $0.0000025/GiB-s. Requests capped at 60 min, so a session must be one long request or many short ones.

modes.label: Services/Jobs, instance-based billing, second-gen execution environment (microVM VM sandbox), Tier 1
modes.note: $0.000018/vCPU-s, $0.000002/GiB-s; whole instance lifetime billed, 1-minute minimum; no per-request fee. Tier 1 includes us-central1/us-east1/us-east4, europe-north1/west1/west4/southwest1/west9, asia-south1/northeast1/east1. GPU non-zonal-redundant L4 $0.0001867/s, RTX PRO 6000 $0.00036522/s. Cloud Run Jobs (run-to-completion tasks, up to 168 h/task) bill at these same instance-based rates with a 1-minute minimum; the separate jobs regime was merged here (identical price). Second-generation execution environment (microVM, full Linux compatibility incl. all syscalls/namespaces/cgroups, NFS): same pricing as first generation per docs; requires at least 512 MiB memory. Jobs and worker pools always use it.

modes.label: Cloud Run CUD 1y/3y, instance-based
modes.commit_note: Cloud Run CUD: commit a $/hour spend for 1y or 3y (same rate, 17% off); applies only to Cloud Run.

modes.label: Compute Flexible CUD 1y, instance-based
modes.commit_note: Compute Flexible CUD 1y spend commitment shared with GCE/GKE; 28% off.

modes.label: Worker pools (no ingress, always-on background), Tier 1
modes.note: $0.000011244/vCPU-s, $0.000001235/GiB-s (identical to Fargate x86). No inbound HTTP; instances up to 7 days continuous (earlier research). Worker pools are manually scaled and billed for every provisioned instance for as long as it exists (pricing page example: one instance "for an entire month"), so the regime is priced as always-on only.

modes.label: Delayed Jobs (deferred start, dynamic price)
modes.note: $0.0000126/vCPU-s, $0.0000014/GiB-s (30% off jobs); "prices are dynamic and can change up to once every 30 days". Flex CUD 3y $0.000006804/$0.000000756.

plans.name: Pay-as-you-go
plans.note: Services: 60-min max request; jobs 168 h per task (1 h with GPU). No platform fee.

perf_source: benchmarks.json computesdk: cold_start_tti median 583.54 ms (2026-08-07), burst_tti median 492.87 ms (2026-09-25); dax never succeeded.

knobs.label: Share of session time with a request in flight (request-based billing)
knobs.why: Request-based billing charges only while a request is being handled (plus start/stop); an agent session that is idle between requests pays nothing for the gaps.

caveats: Rates from the official pricing page tables (raw/cloud_google_com_run_pricing.txt, us-central1 view). The Cloud Billing Catalog API needs an API key and was not used.

Tier 2 regions (europe-west2/3/6/10/12, asia-southeast1/2, asia-east2, asia-northeast3, australia-*, northamerica-*, southamerica-*, us-west2/3/4, me-central*) cost more; exact Tier 2 rates were not captured (page shows the us-central1 view). Cheapest EU/Asia regions are Tier 1 = US price, so region modes collapse into one.

Free tier (per billing account, monthly, applied as a Tier 1 spend discount): instance-based services and jobs 240,000 vCPU-s + 450,000 GiB-s ($5.22 derived = free.monthly_credit); request-based 180,000 vCPU-s + 360,000 GiB-s + 2M requests ($6.02); delayed jobs 342,857 vCPU-s + 642,857 GiB-s; worker pools 384,204 vCPU-s + 728,744 GiB-s. $300 new-customer trial credit is generic GCP (not re-verified this session).

Egress: Premium Tier only; 1 GiB/month free within North America, then $0.12/GiB (0-1 TiB) to NA/EU/Asia, $0.11 (1-10 TiB), $0.08 NA / $0.085 EU-Asia above 10 TiB; Australia/South America/Korea/Indonesia $0.19 then $0.18/$0.15; China $0.23. Same-region traffic to GCP services, Cloud CDN and Cloud Load Balancing is free.
Static egress IP requires Serverless VPC Access or Direct VPC egress + Cloud NAT (NAT pricing not captured). No public IPv4 per instance.
Ephemeral disk (optional) $0.000109589/GiB-h (~$0.08/GiB-month); flex CUD 1y $0.000078904, 3y $0.000059178. The default filesystem is in-memory and counts against RAM.
GPU zonal-redundant surcharge: L4 $0.0002909/s ($1.047/h), RTX PRO 6000 $0.00056913/s ($2.049/h); modes use non-zonal rates. GPU services need >= 4 vCPU/16 GiB (L4) or 20 vCPU/80 GiB (RTX PRO 6000).
The "Instances" table on the pricing page ($0.00000027/vCPU-s, $0.00000193/GiB-s) has no explanation on the page; not modelled.
CUD modes are modelled as always-on commitments; delayed-jobs prices can change every 30 days.

fleet.notes: Regional project CPU/memory/GPU pools, not request concurrency, bound aggregate instances. Published limits depend on region/configuration; request quota in Cloud Quotas. Per-service max-instances setting is not a guaranteed fresh-account fleet allowance.
